value: d=-1 disjoint-cycle sector below the path is NON-EMPTY on the reference (N_{-1}=1.040e8 > 0)
label: reproduces
notes: the deficit grading extends to d=-1 -- pure disjoint-cycle configurations (no degree-1 vertices, |alpha|=m > L+1) strictly BELOW the shortest path in the matched-activity energy landscape. Non-empty means the energy function alone does not put the path at the bottom of the matched-activity space; the drive removes this sector dynamically (it acts on beta, never appearing in the static energy). Prevalence + energy gap: CYC-PREV / CYC-RHO.

value: d=-1 cheaper-cycle prevalence (144 subsample): present 96/absent 25/undetermined 23; per family present sparse 100%/dense 100%/grid 0%/mtn_knn 67%
label: reproduces
notes: two-sided rigorous certificates: ABSENT = sum(m lightest edges) >= w_max+W* (no m-edge set beats it); PRESENT = a heuristic exhibits a disjoint-cycle set on exactly m edges below w_max+W*; UNDETERMINED = neither (a heuristic miss is NOT proof of absence, never imputed). The cheaper-cycle sector is typical on random/terrain weights, absent on the lattice. Reference sanity: present, W_cyc=1.2239, gap@c4=-1.281.

value: rho-law: absence-cert == (gamma>=[L+1/(2rho)]/(L+2)), identity on 144; threshold=1 iff rho=1/4 (L-indep); gamma<=1 on all 144; confusion perfect (25/25)
label: reproduces
notes: the d=-1 absence certificate rewritten via rho=mu/2w_max and gamma=mean(m lightest)/mu is an algebraic identity; the threshold crosses 1 exactly at rho=1/4 for ANY L. So rho<1/4 -> the cheaper-cycle sector is UNAVOIDABLE (absence needs gamma>1, impossible), rho>=1/4 -> possible (only the near-uniform lattice fires). The fourth design coupling: the same rho that buys absence drives the discrimination margin (1-2rho)L+1 to its floor. gamma<=1 is MEASURED on this 144-instance population, NOT a theorem -- an optimum drawn entirely from the graph's lightest edges would violate it.

label: reproduces
